connections.edgeLabel: UK-commissioned study of its own air defence region
connections.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in the UK Air Defence Region (DIS Scientific & Technical Memorandum 55/2/00)
connections.note: The report is DI55's, and its title fixes its scope: 'Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in the UK Air Defence Region', completed in 2000. From that point onwards DI55 was removed from the distribution list of UFO reports received by the MoD. It is a state-commissioned assessment of the phenomenon over British territory with no American equivalent released to the public.

connections.label: Rendlesham Forest Incident, RAF Woodbridge/Bentwaters
connections.note: The National Archives records that the sightings 'took place over two nights late in December 1980 at RAF Woodbridge' in Suffolk, reported by USAF personnel stationed there. That the reports were made at this location is documented; the nature of what was seen remains unresolved.

desc: The United Kingdom occupies a specific argumentative position on this board: it is the state that did what the United States has not. The Ministry of Defence operated a UFO reporting desk from 1950 until December 2009, commissioned the classified Project Condign study of unidentified aerial phenomena in the UK air defence region, and subsequently released its entire UFO file series into the National Archives in successive public tranches. The Rendlesham Forest events of December 1980, involving US Air Force personnel at RAF Woodbridge and Bentwaters, remain the most heavily documented Anglo-American case. Nothing in the British release produced the harms the American concealment case depends on.
